model.rationale: Goldman holds a solidly Republican Fort Worth-area seat, is renominated, and has raised $1.8 million with no outside opposition, while markets give the Democrat about a 4% chance. With no polls or ratings to move the forecast, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly R+15 stands.

overview:
TX-12 covers the Fort Worth area and leans Republican by about 11 points. Craig Goldman, the Republican incumbent, was renominated and enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised about $1.8 million and holding $1.5 million on hand, plus modest outside support and none against him. Democrat Angela Rodriguez Prilliman has no reported fundraising figures and faces a steep structural disadvantage in the seat.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Republicans. Prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 95%. The race is rated Likely Republican, with the Democrat needing an unusual shift in the political environment to compete.
